Thanks for the flag — a few clarifications from Sales Ops and Finance alignments: 

Invoice and PO handling:
- We can include a PO number on any invoice we issue (hosted or marketplace). If purchased through AWS Marketplace, invoicing is routed differently (AWS issues the invoice to the buyer and we receive settlement from AWS). We can surface the PO on the AWS purchase record but AP will still typically want their internal PO on their invoice for reconciliation; we should confirm whether Acme's AP will accept the AWS invoice as-is.
- For direct purchases (PO to Redwood), our billing template supports: invoice number, invoice date, PO number, itemized lines (pilot subscription, overage), billing address, tax ID, remittance instructions. I'll attach a sample invoice PDF.

Net terms and approvals:
- Standard net terms out of the box are net-30.
- We can offer net-45 after a light credit check and finance approval (no exec signoff).
- Net-60 requires VP approval and a business justification (volume + strategic account). If Acme is a reference/customer and plans to expand, we can escalate for net-60 — Vivek can weigh in on the strategic ask.

Vendor form & vendor setup:
- Vendor form looks standard; confirm legal entity address. We will need a W-9 for US tax setup (EIN provided is good).
- Remittance: we can support ACH and wire. If they require a specific remittance reference, note it on the invoice.

Action items from our side:
1) Ben — please confirm whether Acme will attempt Marketplace first or proceed with a direct PO. If Marketplace, ask AP if they'll accept the AWS invoice for reconciliation or still require a PO to be attached to the invoice.
2) Marissa (Sales Ops) — attaching sample_invoice_sample.pdf and the vendor onboarding checklist for AP.
3) Finance — I'll start a light credit check for Acme if they request net-45; Ben, let me know if you want me to escalate for net-60 and I can prepare justification notes.

Attachments: sample_invoice_sample.pdf, vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf
